'''Eleftherios Ν. Economou''' ({{langx|el|Ελευθέριος Ν. Οικονόμου|Elefthérios N. Oikonómou}}; born 7 February 1940) is a [[Greeks|Greek]] theoretical physicist and professor emeritus at the department of physics<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.uoc.gr/en/faculty/e.economou|title=Economou Eleftherios {{!}} Department of Physics|website=www.physics.uoc.gr|access-date=2020-04-01}}</ref> of the [[University of Crete]]. He has contributed to various areas of theoretical condensed matter physics, starting with the study of [[surface plasmon]]s during his thesis in 1969.

Economou influenced the evolution of theoretical physics in Greece since the late 1970s, as described in detail in a special volume published in 2000, in ''[[Physica B]]'', on the occasion on his 60th birthday.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Sifakis|first=Grigoris M.|date=2001-02-01|title=E.N. Economou's contribution to the establishment and development of the University of Crete and the Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0921452600007547|journal=Physica B: Condensed Matter|series=Proceedings of the Symposium on Wave Propagation and Electronic Structure in Disordered Systems|language=en|volume=296|issue=1|pages=1–6|doi=10.1016/S0921-4526(00)00754-7|bibcode=2001PhyB..296....1S|issn=0921-4526|url-access=subscription}}</ref> His opinion perspective is still solicited<ref>{{Cite journal|date=August 2013|title=The road ahead for research in Greece|journal=Nature Materials|language=en|volume=12|issue=8|page=681|doi=10.1038/nmat3735|pmid=23877386|bibcode=2013NatMa..12..681.|issn=1476-4660|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|date=August 2013|title=Tough times for Greek science|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/nmat3726|journal=Nature Materials|language=en|volume=12|issue=8|pages=686–687|doi=10.1038/nmat3726|pmid=23877388|issn=1476-4660|last1=Economou|first1=E.|bibcode=2013NatMa..12..686.|url-access=subscription}}</ref> by major science journals, such as ''[[Nature Materials]]'', in particular on how to address challenges related to effects of economic crisis in Greece in science and technology. He contributed substantially to shaping the first steps of the University of Crete<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cup.gr/book/panepistimio-kritis-i-genesi-ke-i-poria-1977-2017/|title=Πανεπιστήμιο Κρήτης: Η γένεση και η πορεία, 1977–2017|date=2018-06-01|website=Πανεπιστημιακές Εκδόσεις Κρήτης|language=el|access-date=2020-03-31}}</ref> and led the effort in creating the [[Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas]] (FORTH), serving as its first director general from its foundation in 1983 until 2004. He has been teaching in the department of physics of the University of Crete since 1982 and also wrote 13 textbooks, mostly in topics related to theoretical physics and condensed matter physics. He has published over 300 refereed papers,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://publons.com/researcher/2834701/eleftherios-n-economou/|title=Eleftherios N. Economou's Publons profile|website=publons.com|language=en|access-date=2020-04-03}}</ref> which have received more than 29,000 citations according to [[Google Scholar]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.gr/citations?user=5PI1_AIAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Eleftherios N. Economou – Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.gr|access-date=2020-04-01}}</ref>

== Early years ==
Eleftherios Economou was born in Athens, Greece on February 7, 1940. He grew up in a working-class neighbourhood of [[Kallithea]] and his early years, along with his parents Nikos and Sophia and his younger brother Vassilis, were influenced by [[World War II]] and in particular by the [[Greek Civil War]] that followed. In 1952 he was admitted to the selective public Experimental School of the University of Athens, from where he graduated in 1958. The same year he was admitted in the School of Electrical & Mechanical Engineering of the [[National Technical University of Athens]]. Among his classmates was [[John Iliopoulos]], A theoretical physicist. He graduated with first class honours in 1963 and commenced the compulsory, in Greece, military service, which at the time lasted two and a half years. During this period, he was given the opportunity to attend a number of graduate level physics courses at the "Center for Advanced Studies and Philosophy of Science" which was organised at the [[National Centre of Scientific Research "Demokritos"]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

In 1965 Economou applied for graduate studies in the U.S. and was admitted to the department of physics of the [[University of Chicago]]. Before leaving for the U.S., in February 1966, he married Athanasia Paganou<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/peopleinfo.php?pid=810942|title=Chemistry Tree – Athanasia L. Paganou|website=academictree.org|access-date=2020-04-06}}</ref> and they have a daughter, [[Sophia Economou]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.phys.vt.edu/About/people/Faculty/sophia-economou.html|title=Sophia Economou|website=www.phys.vt.edu|language=en|access-date=2020-04-02}}</ref> who is professor of physics at [[Virginia Tech|Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University]]. He arrived in Chicago in 1966. Two months later he passed the qualifying exams, ranking first among his classmates, which made it easy<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Cohen|first=Morrel H.|date=2001-02-01|title=E.N. Economou and the metal-to-insulator transition|url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0921452600007729|journal=Physica B: Condensed Matter|series=Proceedings of the Symposium on Wave Propagation and Electronic Structure in Disordered Systems|language=en|volume=296|issue=1|pages=7–20|doi=10.1016/S0921-4526(00)00772-9|bibcode=2001PhyB..296....7C|issn=0921-4526|url-access=subscription}}</ref> to be accepted as a PhD student in the group of [[Morrel H. Cohen]]. Economou decided to focus on theoretical condensed matter physics. He completed his studies and was awarded a PhD in three years with a dissertation entitled, "Surface Plasmons in Thin Films"<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Economou|first=E. N.|date=1969-06-10|title=Surface Plasmons in Thin Films|journal=Physical Review|volume=182|issue=2|pages=539–554|doi=10.1103/physrev.182.539|bibcode=1969PhRv..182..539E|issn=0031-899X}}</ref> in 1969.

== Scientific career ==
Economou became assistant professor and later professor in the department of physics at the [[University of Virginia]] (1970–1981). He has been visiting professor at the University of Chicago (1994), [[University of Lausanne|Université de Lausanne]] (1992), [[Princeton University]] (1978), [[Iowa State &nbsp;University]] (1991–1992) and an affiliated member of [[Ames Laboratory]] since 1992. He was visiting researcher at the [[National Centre of Scientific Research "Demokritos"]] (1997–1998) &nbsp;and a &nbsp;Chair Professor of Theoretical Physics at the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens|University of Athens]] (1978–1981). In 1981 he and P. Lambropoulos were the first elected professors in the newly founded department of physics of the University of Crete (Greece). As the acting chairman of the department<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.uoc.gr/el/committees|title=Διοίκηση και Επιτροπές Τμήματος Φυσικής {{!}} Τμήμα Φυσικής|website=www.physics.uoc.gr|access-date=2020-04-16}}</ref> he established the bases in the Physics &nbsp;curriculum and he was instrumental<ref name=":3" /> in hiring high quality faculty at the University of Crete. He was and remains a strong advocate on topics related to the negative influence of political parties and direct involvement of students in the normal operation of the universities.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.patris.gr/articles/101881/51036|title=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ – ΑΡΧΕΙΟ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΕΚΔΟΣΗΣ|website=archive.patris.gr|access-date=2020-04-13}}</ref> He retired in 2007,<ref name=":15">{{Cite web|url=https://archive.patris.gr/articles/63578|title=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ – ΑΡΧΕΙΟ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΕΚΔΟΣΗΣ|website=archive.patris.gr|access-date=2020-04-13}}</ref><ref name=":16">{{Cite web|url=https://archive.patris.gr/articles/169816|title=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ – ΑΡΧΕΙΟ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΕΚΔΟΣΗΣ|website=archive.patris.gr|access-date=2020-04-13}}</ref> and still serves and teaches in the department of physics as professor emeritus.

Economou was the prominent figure of a group of five Greek scientists from abroad, namely [[Fotis Kafatos]], [https://geschichte.univie.ac.at/en/persons/dionysios-dennis-tsichritzis-prof-dr Dionysios (Dennis) Tsichritzis], Grigoris Sifakis<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nyu.academia.edu/GrigorisSifakis|title=Grigoris Sifakis {{!}} New York University – Academia.edu|website=nyu.academia.edu|access-date=2020-04-02}}{{Dead link|date=March 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> and Peter (Panagiotis) Lambropoulos,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.physics.uoc.gr/en/faculty/p.lambropoulos|title=Lambropoulos Panagiotis {{!}} Department of Physics|website=www.physics.uoc.gr|access-date=2020-04-03}}</ref> who planned the idea<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.patris.gr/2017/11/20/erevnitiki-kinotita-apochereta-ton-pagkosmio-ellina/|title=Η ερευνητική κοινότητα αποχαιρετά τον παγκόσμιο Έλληνα|date=2017-11-20|website=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ|language=el|access-date=2020-04-13}}</ref> and with the help of the Minister of Research and Technology [[Georgios Lianis]], convinced the Greek Government to create<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":1" /> the first three Institutes of the&nbsp;Research Center of Crete (RCC; Ερευνητικό Κέντρο Κρήτης – ΕΚΕΚ)&nbsp;in [[Heraklion]]. &nbsp;During his leadership as its first director general (1983–2004),<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.patris.gr/2017/11/20/erevnitiki-kinotita-apochereta-ton-pagkosmio-ellina/3088-2/|title=Ο πρώτος πρόεδρος του ΙΤΕ, κ. Λευτέρης Οικονόμου|website=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ|language=el|access-date=2020-04-13}}</ref> RCC expanded with the Institute of Mediterranean Studies (IMS) in [[Rethymno]] and the Institute of Applied Computational Mathematics in Heraklion. In 1986 [[Skinakas Observatory]], jointly supported by RCC, the [[University of Crete]] and the [[Max Planck Institute for Extraterrestrial Physics]] (Germany) also commenced its operations. In 1987 with the agreement of George Papatheodorou<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prof. George Papatheodorou, ICE-HT/FORTH|url=http://www.iceht.forth.gr/staff/papatheodorou.html|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040712055802/http://www.iceht.forth.gr/staff/papatheodorou.html|archive-date=2004-07-12}}</ref> and Iacovos Vasalos<ref>{{Cite web|title=Iacovos Vasalos Home Page|url=http://www.vasalos.com/|website=www.vasalos.com|access-date=2020-05-05}}</ref> Directors of the Institute of Chemical Engineering & High Temperature Processes - (ICE/HT) in [[Patras]], and the Chemical Process Engineering Research Institute (CPERI) [[Thessaloniki]], the two Institutes joined RCC and the &nbsp;[[Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas]] (FORTH) was created. In 2000 CPERI was renamed Centre for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH) becoming independent of FORTH. In 2002 the Biomedical Research Institute (BRI), based in Ioannina was incorporated into FORTH. In parallel, with financial support from the [[European Union]], the construction of the FORTH buildings in Heraklion, Patras, Thessaloniki, and the restoration of the IMS building in Rethymno began. Science and Technology Parks were established connected to the institutes in Heraklion, Patras, and Thessaloniki and respective buildings with European funding were erected. The main FORTH building infrastructure in Heraklion in 2004 had an area of 30,000 square meters. Most of the buildings were designed<ref>{{Cite web|title=Panos Koulermos: Research Centre Of Crete and University Of Crete|url=http://www.koulermos.com/resrch.htm|website=www.koulermos.com|access-date=2020-05-04}}</ref> and supervised by Panos Koulermos,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Panos Koulermos: Biography|url=http://www.koulermos.com/bio.htm|website=www.koulermos.com|access-date=2020-05-04}}</ref> then a professor of architecture at the [[University of Southern California]]. FORTH has been established as the premier research organisation in Greece,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.patris.gr/articles/27532/6318|title=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ – ΑΡΧΕΙΟ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΕΚΔΟΣΗΣ|website=archive.patris.gr|access-date=2020-04-13}}</ref> ranking consistently first in scientific quality and international recognition by a variety of metrics,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://research.webometrics.info/en/Europe/Greece|title=Greece {{!}} Ranking Web of Research Centers|website=research.webometrics.info|access-date=2020-04-04}}</ref> including evaluations by external Committees as well as attracting funding by [[European Research Council]] grants. Achieving this status was not easy, as several times the supervising agencies attempted to introduce political criteria and to intervene.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.patris.gr/articles/25361|title=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ – ΑΡΧΕΙΟ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΕΚΔΟΣΗΣ|website=archive.patris.gr|access-date=2020-04-16}}</ref>

Economou stepped down from the position of director general of FORTH in April 2004,<ref name=":16" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://archive.patris.gr/articles/27532/6316|title=ΠΑΤΡΙΣ – ΑΡΧΕΙΟ ΗΛΕΚΤΡΟΝΙΚΗΣ ΕΚΔΟΣΗΣ|website=archive.patris.gr|access-date=2020-04-23}}</ref> and he was succeeded<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ercim.eu/publication/Ercim_News/enw57/ib1.html|title=Stelios C. Orphanoudakis has been elected as the new Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Foundation for Research and Technology-Hellas|website=www.ercim.eu|access-date=2020-04-23}}</ref> by Stelios C. Orphanoudakis. Three years later, in 2007, he reached the compulsory retirement age of 67 at the university. He was awarded<ref name=":15" /> the title of emeritus professor at the University of Crete. He continued to teach until 2024 and he still remains active in research. A symposium on his honor entitled "From electrons to elastic and electromagnetic waves<ref>{{Cite web |title=From electrons to elastic and electromagnetic waves |url=https://economou85.iesl.forth.gr/ |access-date=2025-07-01 |language=en-US}}</ref>" was organized on June 30, 2025 on the occasion of his 85th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Σύνταξης |first=Αίθουσα |date=2025-06-30 |title=Συγκίνηση στο ΙΤΕ για τα 85 χρόνια του Ελευθερίου Ν. Οικονόμου |url=https://www.patris.gr/ekpaidefsi/sto-ite-gia-ta-85-xronia-tou-eleftheriou-n-oikonomou/ |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=PATRIS.GR |language=el}}</ref>

== Research areas ==
Economou worked in a broad range of topics in the area of [[condensed matter physics]]. These topics include electronic properties of many different [[material]]s and systems, with emphasis on systems with defects ([[crystallographic defect]]s) and disordered systems (e.g. amorphous [[Semiconductor|semiconductors)]],<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Soukoulis|first1=C. Since 1990 Economou's research is mainly focused on electromagnetic and acoustic/elastic wave propagation in complex systems. He was one of the initiators of the field of phononic crystals (i.e. acoustic/elastic wave [[band gap]] materials) which led to the more recent and wider field of [[acoustic metamaterial]]s. His 1992 publication «Elastic and acoustic wave band structure»,<ref name=":6" /> was one of the two (almost simultaneous) publications discussing for the first time the concept of the acoustic band gap. This paper was followed by many other well-recognized of Economou's works in the field of phononic crystals and elastic wave propagation in complex systems (see <ref name=":8" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":9" /><ref name=":10" />).

In the field of electromagnetic metamaterials, Economou's research helped to eliminate some of the first objections of the scientific community on the possibility of the existence of [[Negative-index metamaterial]]s,<ref name=":11" /> revealing the possibility and limitations for the achievement of negative [[refractive index]] in the [[Visible spectrum|optical spectrum]],<ref name=":12" /> and demonstrating some of the unique properties and capabilities of metamaterials (e.g. the possibility for achievement of repulsive [[Casimir effect|Casimir force]] in chiral metamaterials<ref name=":13" />). In his research on metamaterials, Economou works in close collaboration with his long-term colleague [[Costas Soukoulis]], since the period 1979 to 1982 when Soukoulis was a [[postdoctoral researcher]] under his supervision<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=226239|title=Physics Tree – Costas M. Soukoulis|website=academictree.org|access-date=2020-04-15}}</ref> at the University of Virginia. The collaborative research on negative index metamaterials led by Economou and Soukoulis, including scientists from [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]] (Sir [[John Pendry]]), [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]] and [[Bilkent University]] ([[Ekmel Özbay]]), was recognized with the award of the [[European Union]] [[Descartes Prize|Descartes prize]] for collaborative research in 2005.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

One of the most important scientific contributions by Economou is considered his PhD work on [[surface plasmon]]s. The relevant 1969 publication "Surface plasmons in thin films",<ref name=":0" /> among the first of his career, has become a reference work for the modern field of [[plasmonics]].{{citation needed|date=June 2020}}

Among Economou's earlier research, quite important is considered{{by whom|date=June 2020}} also the research on [[Anderson localization]] in systems with defects (i.e., [[crystallographic defect]]) and disordered systems.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7" /> Many of the novel and important results of this research are summarized in his book "Green's Functions in Quantum Physics".

== Books ==
Economou has written several physics textbooks in Greek and in English. His book ''Green's functions in Quantum Physics'', originally published in 1979, has received more than 2500 citations according to [[Google Scholar]]. It was included in the electronic Springer Book Archives containing 40 renowned imprints published by Springer between 1842 and 2005.
